{{Short description|Faithfully flat morphism of schemes}}
{{lowercase title}}
In [[algebraic geometry]], there are two slightly different definitions of an '''fpqc morphism''', both variations of [[faithfully flat morphism]]s of [[scheme (mathematics)|scheme]]s. 

Sometimes an fpqc morphism means one that is faithfully flat and [[quasi-compact morphism|quasi-compact]]. This is where the abbreviation fpqc comes from: fpqc stands for the [[French language|French]] phrase "fidèlement plat et quasi-compacte", meaning "faithfully flat and quasi-compact".

However, it is more common to define an fpqc morphism <math>f: X \to Y</math> of schemes to be a faithfully flat morphism that satisfies the following equivalent conditions:
# Every [[quasi-compact]] open subset of <math>Y</math> is the image of a quasi-compact open subset of <math>X</math>.
# There exists a covering <math>V_i</math> of <math>Y</math> by open affine subschemes such that each <math>V_i</math> is the image of a quasi-compact open subset of <math>X</math>.
# Each point <math>x \in X</math> has a neighborhood <math>U</math> such that <math>f(U)</math> is open and <math>f: U \to f(U)</math> is quasi-compact.
# Each point <math>x \in X</math> has a quasi-compact neighborhood <math>U</math> such that <math>f(U)</math> is open affine.

Examples: An open faithfully flat morphism is fpqc.

An fpqc morphism satisfies the following properties:
* The composite of fpqc morphisms is fpqc.
* A [[Base change (scheme theory)|base change]] of an fpqc morphism is fpqc.
* If <math>f: X \to Y</math> is a morphism of schemes and if there is an open covering <math>V_i</math> of <math>Y</math> such that the <math>f: f^{-1}(V_i) \to V_i</math> is fpqc, then <math>f</math> is fpqc.
* A faithfully flat morphism that is locally of finite presentation (i.e., fppf) is fpqc.
* If <math>f:X \to Y</math> is an fpqc morphism, a subset of <math>Y</math> is open in <math>Y</math> if and only if its inverse image under <math>f</math> is open in <math>X</math>.
